concatenation-of-array: Return a new array containing two consecutive copies of nums, preserving the order of each copy.
contains-duplicate: Determine whether nums contains any repeated value. Return True for a duplicate and False when all values are distinct.
valid-anagram: Decide whether s and t contain exactly the same characters with the same frequencies.
two-sum: Find two different indices in nums whose values sum to target. Return either ordering of those indices. The input has exactly one valid pair.
longest-common-prefix: Return the longest starting substring shared by every string in strs. Return an empty string if no character is shared at the start.
group-anagrams: Partition strs into groups of anagrams. Every input string must appear once; group order and the order within each group do not matter.
remove-element: Remove every occurrence of val from nums in place. Return the number k of retained values and place those values in the first k positions. Their order does not matter.
majority-element: Return the value that occurs more than half the time in nums. Such a value is guaranteed to exist.
design-hashset: Implement MyHashSet with add(key), remove(key), and contains(key). Adding an existing key or removing an absent key must be safe. Do not delegate storage to a built-in set.
design-hashmap: Implement MyHashMap with put(key, value), get(key), and remove(key). Updating a key replaces its value. get returns -1 for absent keys. Do not use a built-in hash map as the implementation.
sort-an-array: Return nums sorted in ascending order. Implement the sorting algorithm yourself, targeting O(n log n) time.
sort-colors: Rearrange nums in place so all 0 values precede all 1 values, which precede all 2 values. Use constant extra space and avoid a library sorting function.
top-k-frequent-elements: Return the k values with the highest frequencies in nums. The selected set is unique, and its output order does not matter.
encode-and-decode-strings: Implement encode(strings) and decode(encoded). Encoding must produce one string; decoding it must recover the exact original list, including empty strings and delimiter characters. Do not use an in-memory lookup to retain the original input.
range-sum-query-2d-immutable: Implement NumMatrix(matrix) and sumRegion(row1, col1, row2, col2). Each query returns the sum of the inclusive rectangle between the two corners. The matrix does not change between queries.
product-of-array-except-self: Return an array whose value at i is the product of every nums element except nums[i]. Do not use division. Target linear time.
valid-sudoku: Check a partially filled 9 by 9 Sudoku board. Each row, column, and 3 by 3 box must have no repeated digit from 1 through 9. A dot denotes an empty cell; you need not solve the board.
longest-consecutive-sequence: Find the length of the longest run of consecutive integer values present in nums. Input order is irrelevant. Target O(n) time.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-ii: Return the largest profit from any number of stock transactions. Hold at most one share at a time, selling before buying another. Each price belongs to the corresponding day.
majority-element-ii: Return every number appearing more than floor(n / 3) times in nums. Output order does not matter.
subarray-sum-equals-k: Count the nonempty contiguous subarrays of nums whose sum is k. Values may be negative or zero.
first-missing-positive: Return the smallest positive integer absent from nums. Use O(n) time and constant auxiliary space.
reverse-string: Reverse the character array s in place with constant extra space.
valid-palindrome: Ignore non-alphanumeric characters and letter case, then decide whether s reads the same forward and backward.
valid-palindrome-ii: Decide whether s can become a palindrome after deleting at most one character.
merge-strings-alternately: Build a string by alternating characters from word1 and word2, starting with word1. Append the rest of the longer string when the other runs out.
merge-sorted-array: Merge the first m values of nums1 and the n values of nums2 into sorted order inside nums1. Its remaining n positions are reserved space, not additional input values.
remove-duplicates-from-sorted-array: Compact a sorted nums array in place so each distinct value appears once at the beginning, in sorted order. Return the number of distinct values.
two-sum-ii-input-array-is-sorted: Find two distinct positions in an ascending array whose values sum to target. Return their 1-based indices in increasing order. Exactly one pair exists. Use constant extra space.
3sum: Return all distinct triples of values in nums that sum to zero. A triple must use three different indices. Neither triple ordering nor result ordering matters.
4sum: Return the distinct quadruples of values in nums that sum to target, using four different indices per quadruple. Output order does not matter.
rotate-array: Rotate nums in place to the right by k steps. Values shifted beyond the end wrap to the beginning.
container-with-most-water: Choose two heights whose vertical lines form a container with the x-axis. Return the maximum possible area: the smaller height times the distance between indices.
boats-to-save-people: Find the fewest boats needed to transport people. Each boat holds at most two people and their combined weight cannot exceed limit. Every individual fits on a boat.
trapping-rain-water: Treat height as unit-width elevation bars. Return the total volume of water retained between the bars after rainfall.
contains-duplicate-ii: Return True if nums has equal values at two different indices whose distance is at most k; otherwise return False.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock: Find the maximum profit from buying one share and selling it on a later day. Return zero if every possible transaction loses money.
longest-substring-without-repeating-char: Return the length of the longest contiguous substring of s containing no repeated character.
longest-repeating-character-replacement: You may replace at most k characters in s. Find the maximum length of a contiguous substring that can be made entirely one repeated character.
permutation-in-string: Decide whether s2 contains a contiguous substring that is a permutation of s1.
minimum-size-subarray-sum: For an array of positive integers, return the minimum length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is at least target. Return zero if no subarray qualifies.
find-k-closest-elements: Return the k values of sorted arr closest to x, in ascending order. Prefer the smaller value when distances tie.
minimum-window-substring: Find the shortest substring of s containing every character of t with its required frequency. Return an empty string if no window exists. A nonempty minimum answer is unique.
sliding-window-maximum: For each contiguous window of k values in nums, return its maximum, in left-to-right window order.
baseball-game: Evaluate the score record operations. An integer adds a score; + adds the sum of the previous two; D doubles the previous score; C removes the previous score. Return the final total. Operations are valid.
valid-parentheses: Check a string of parentheses, square brackets, and braces. Every closing symbol must match the most recent unmatched opening symbol, and none may remain unmatched.
implement-stack-using-queues: Implement MyStack with push, pop, top, and empty, using queue operations internally. pop removes the most recently pushed value; top reads it.
implement-queue-using-stacks: Implement MyQueue with push, pop, peek, and empty, using stack operations internally. pop removes the oldest remaining value; peek reads it.
min-stack: Implement MinStack supporting push, pop, top, and getMin. Each operation must take O(1) time; getMin returns the smallest value currently stored.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation: Evaluate tokens in reverse Polish notation using +, -, *, and /. Integer division truncates toward zero. The expression is valid and has no division by zero.
asteroid-collision: Positive asteroids move right and negative asteroids move left. On collision the smaller absolute value disappears; equal sizes both disappear. Return the survivors in their original relative order.
daily-temperatures: For each day's temperature, return how many days must pass before a warmer temperature. Use zero if no later day is warmer.
online-stock-span: Implement StockSpanner.next(price). Return the number of consecutive days ending today whose prices are at most today's price, including today itself.
car-fleet: Cars travel toward target from distinct positions with given speeds. A faster car that catches one ahead joins its fleet and cannot pass. Count the fleets that reach target; meeting exactly at target counts as one fleet.
simplify-path: Normalize an absolute Unix path. Ignore repeated slashes and dot segments; a double dot moves to the parent unless already at root. Other names are ordinary directory names.
decode-string: Decode nested expressions of the form k[sequence], repeating the enclosed sequence k times. Literal letters remain in order. The encoding is valid.
maximum-frequency-stack: Implement FreqStack.push(val) and pop(). pop removes the most frequent value; among equally frequent values, remove the most recently pushed one.
largest-rectangle-in-histogram: Given unit-width bar heights, return the largest rectangular area that fits under consecutive bars.
binary-search: Find target in ascending nums using binary search. Return its index, or -1 when it is absent.
search-insert-position: Return target's index in a sorted array, or the index where inserting it would preserve ascending order. Use logarithmic time.
guess-number-higher-or-lower: Find the hidden integer from 1 through n using guess(value). The API returns -1 when your guess is too high, 1 when too low, and 0 when correct. The test's pick value configures the API and is not a method parameter.
sqrtx: Return the integer part of the nonnegative square root of x without using square-root or fractional-exponent library operations.
search-a-2d-matrix: Determine whether target occurs in a matrix whose rows are sorted and whose first value in each row is greater than the previous row's last value. Target logarithmic search time.
koko-eating-bananas: Find the smallest integer eating speed that finishes all piles within h hours. During an hour, eat from only one pile, up to that speed; unused capacity is lost.
capacity-to-ship-packages-within-d-days: Find the smallest ship capacity that can deliver weights within days. Ship packages in their given order, splitting them into consecutive daily loads.
find-minimum-in-rotated-sorted-array: Return the minimum value in an ascending array of distinct values that has been rotated. Target logarithmic time.
search-in-rotated-sorted-array: Find target's index in a rotated ascending array of distinct values, or return -1. Use O(log n) time.
search-in-rotated-sorted-array-ii: Decide whether target is present in a rotated nondecreasing array. Duplicate values are allowed.
time-based-key-value-store: Implement TimeMap.set(key, value, timestamp) and get(key, timestamp). get returns the value at the largest stored timestamp not exceeding the query, or an empty string. Set timestamps arrive in increasing order.
split-array-largest-sum: Split nums into k nonempty contiguous pieces. Return the smallest achievable value of the largest piece sum. Input values are nonnegative.
median-of-two-sorted-arrays: Return the median of the combined values of two sorted arrays. At least one value exists. Target O(log(m + n)) time.
find-in-mountain-array: Find target's smallest index in an array that strictly rises to a peak and then strictly falls. Access it only through MountainArray.get(index) and length(), using at most 100 get calls. Return -1 when absent.
reverse-linked-list: Reverse a singly linked list and return its new head. The tests represent linked lists as arrays; the method receives ListNode objects.
merge-two-sorted-lists: Merge two ascending linked lists into one ascending list by linking their nodes. Return the merged head.
linked-list-cycle: Determine whether following next pointers eventually revisits a node. The test parameter pos sets the tail's link to a zero-based node index, or -1 for no cycle; the method receives only the head.
reorder-list: Rearrange the list in place into first, last, second, second-last, and so on. Change links rather than node values.
remove-nth-node-from-end-of-list: Remove the nth node counted from the end of a linked list and return the resulting head. n is valid.
copy-list-with-random-pointer: Deep-copy a list whose nodes have next and random pointers. Every copied pointer must refer to a copied node or None. Examples encode each node as [value, random_index].
add-two-numbers: Two linked lists hold nonnegative integers with the least significant digit first. Return their sum as a new list in the same digit order.
find-the-duplicate-number: nums contains n+1 values in the range 1 through n, with one distinct value repeated. Return that value without modifying nums and using constant extra space.
reverse-linked-list-ii: Reverse the nodes between 1-based positions left and right, inclusive. Preserve the rest of the list and return the head.
design-circular-queue: Implement MyCircularQueue(k) with enQueue, deQueue, Front, Rear, isEmpty, and isFull. Insertions and removals return success flags; Front and Rear return -1 when empty.
lru-cache: Implement LRUCache(capacity), get(key), and put(key, value). Reads and writes mark a key as recently used. When full, evict the least recently used key. Missing reads return -1. Target O(1) per operation.
lfu-cache: Implement LFUCache with get and put. Evict the least frequently used key when full, breaking frequency ties by least recent use. New keys start at frequency one; reads and updates increase frequency. Missing reads return -1.
merge-k-sorted-lists: Merge all the ascending linked lists into one ascending linked list. Return None when there are no nodes.
reverse-nodes-in-k-group: Reverse linked-list nodes in consecutive groups of k. Leave a final group shorter than k unchanged. Relink nodes without changing their values.
binary-tree-inorder-traversal: Return binary-tree values in left-subtree, node, right-subtree order.
binary-tree-preorder-traversal: Return binary-tree values in node, left-subtree, right-subtree order.
binary-tree-postorder-traversal: Return binary-tree values in left-subtree, right-subtree, node order.
invert-binary-tree: Swap every node's left and right subtrees and return the root of the mirrored tree.
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree: Return the maximum number of nodes on a root-to-leaf path. An empty tree has depth zero.
diameter-of-binary-tree: Return the greatest number of edges on any path between two nodes of a binary tree. The path need not pass through the root.
balanced-binary-tree: Check whether every node's left and right subtree heights differ by at most one.
same-tree: Return True when two binary trees have the same shape and equal values at corresponding nodes.
subtree-of-another-tree: Determine whether root contains a subtree identical in shape and values to subRoot.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-searc: Return the lowest node that is an ancestor of both p and q in a binary search tree. A node counts as its own ancestor. Both nodes exist and values are unique.
insert-into-a-binary-search-tree: Insert val into a binary search tree while preserving its ordering, and return the root. val is not already present.
delete-node-in-a-bst: Delete the node with key from a binary search tree, preserving its ordering. Return the resulting root; an absent key leaves the tree unchanged.
binary-tree-level-order-traversal: Return the tree's values grouped by depth, from the root downward and from left to right within each level.
binary-tree-right-side-view: Return the last visible node value at each depth when viewing the tree from its right side.
construct-quad-tree: Represent a square binary grid as a quad tree. A uniform region is a leaf with its value; otherwise split it into top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right quadrants. Internal-node values do not matter.
count-good-nodes-in-binary-tree: Count nodes whose value is at least every value on the path from the root to that node, including the node itself.
validate-binary-search-tree: Check whether every node's left subtree contains only smaller values and its right subtree only larger values. Duplicate values violate the ordering.
kth-smallest-element-in-a-bst: Return the kth smallest node value in a binary search tree, counting from one.
construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-: Rebuild the binary tree from its preorder and inorder traversals. All node values are distinct and the traversals describe the same tree.
house-robber-iii: Choose tree nodes with the largest total value, subject to never choosing both a node and its immediate parent. Return that maximum total.
delete-leaves-with-a-given-value: Repeatedly remove leaf nodes whose value equals target, including parents that become matching leaves after removal. Return the remaining root.
binary-tree-maximum-path-sum: Return the maximum sum along a nonempty path in the tree. A path follows parent-child edges without revisiting nodes and may begin and end anywhere.
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree: Implement Codec.serialize(root) and deserialize(data). Serialization produces a string; deserialization must recover the same binary-tree structure and values. No particular string format is required.
kth-largest-element-in-a-stream: Implement KthLargest(k, nums). Each add(val) inserts a value and returns the kth largest value seen so far, counting duplicates separately.
last-stone-weight: Repeatedly smash the two heaviest stones. Equal stones both disappear; unequal stones leave one stone of their weight difference. Return the final weight, or zero.
k-closest-points-to-origin: Return k input points having the smallest squared distances from the origin. Any order is allowed, and equally distant points may be chosen interchangeably.
kth-largest-element-in-an-array: Return the kth largest value in nums, counting duplicate occurrences separately.
task-scheduler: Schedule unit-duration tasks with at least n intervening intervals between occurrences of the same task. You may reorder tasks and insert idle intervals. Return the shortest schedule length.
design-twitter: Implement Twitter with postTweet, getNewsFeed, follow, and unfollow. A feed contains at most ten most recent tweet IDs from the user and followed users, newest first.
single-threaded-cpu: Tasks provide enqueue and processing times. An idle CPU selects the available task with the shortest processing time, breaking ties by original index. Return the processing order of indices.
reorganize-string: Rearrange s so no two adjacent characters match. Return any valid rearrangement, or an empty string when impossible.
longest-happy-string: Build the longest string using at most a copies of a, b copies of b, and c copies of c, with no three identical consecutive characters. Any maximum-length answer is valid.
car-pooling: Each trip specifies passenger count, pickup position, and drop-off position. Decide whether the vehicle can complete all trips without exceeding capacity. Passengers leave before new passengers board at the same position.
find-median-from-data-stream: Implement MedianFinder.addNum(num) and findMedian(). Return the middle stored value, or the mean of the two middle values when the count is even.
ipo: Starting with capital w, choose at most k distinct projects. A project requires its capital threshold to be met, then adds its profit to your capital. Return the maximum final capital.
sum-of-all-subset-xor-totals: For every subset of nums, XOR its elements, treating the empty subset as zero. Return the sum of all these XOR values. Equal values at different indices remain distinct choices.
subsets: Return every subset of the distinct values in nums, including the empty subset. Output order does not matter.
combination-sum: Return unique combinations of candidate values summing to target. Candidates are distinct positive integers and may be reused without limit. Combination order does not matter.
combination-sum-ii: Return unique combinations summing to target using each candidate occurrence at most once. Duplicate input values must not create duplicate combinations.
combinations: Return every choice of k distinct integers from 1 through n. Output order does not matter.
permutations: Return every ordering of the distinct values in nums.
subsets-ii: Return all distinct subsets of nums, which may contain duplicates. Include the empty subset without duplicating equivalent selections.
permutations-ii: Return every distinct ordering of nums, which may contain repeated values.
generate-parentheses: Return every properly balanced string formed using n pairs of parentheses.
word-search: Decide whether word can be traced through orthogonally adjacent cells of board. A cell may be used at most once in one trace.
palindrome-partitioning: Return all ways to split s into nonempty substrings such that every substring is a palindrome. Keep substring order within each partition.
letter-combinations-of-a-phone-number: Return every letter string represented by digits 2 through 9 on a phone keypad. An empty digit string produces an empty list.
matchsticks-to-square: Decide whether all matchsticks can form four sides of equal length. Use every stick once and do not break sticks.
partition-to-k-equal-sum-subsets: Decide whether nums can be partitioned into k nonempty groups with equal sums, using each occurrence exactly once.
n-queens: Return all n by n boards placing n queens so none share a row, column, or diagonal. Use Q for a queen and a dot for an empty cell.
n-queens-ii: Count the distinct placements of n queens on an n by n board with no shared row, column, or diagonal.
word-break-ii: Return all sentences formed by splitting s into dictionary words. Words may be reused. Separate the words of each sentence with single spaces.
implement-trie-prefix-tree: Implement Trie.insert(word), search(word), and startsWith(prefix). search requires an entire inserted word; startsWith only requires a matching prefix.
design-add-and-search-words-data-structu: Implement WordDictionary.addWord(word) and search(pattern). In a search pattern, each dot matches exactly one arbitrary letter.
extra-characters-in-a-string: Split s into nonoverlapping dictionary words and unused characters. Return the smallest possible number of unused characters. Dictionary words may be reused.
word-search-ii: Return all dictionary words traceable through orthogonally adjacent board cells. A cell cannot repeat within one word trace, and each found word appears only once in the result.
island-perimeter: Compute the perimeter of the island in a binary grid. A land edge contributes one when it borders water or the outside of the grid.
verifying-an-alien-dictionary: Decide whether words are in lexicographic order under the given ordering of alphabet characters. A word precedes a longer word for which it is a prefix.
find-the-town-judge: Among people labeled 1 through n, find the person trusted by everyone else who trusts nobody. Return the label or -1 when no such person exists.
number-of-islands: Count groups of '1' cells connected horizontally or vertically in grid. Diagonal contact does not connect islands.
max-area-of-island: Return the largest number of orthogonally connected land cells in a binary grid, or zero when there is no land.
clone-graph: Deep-copy the connected graph reachable from node. Preserve node values and neighbor relationships, with no copied node referring to the original graph.
walls-and-gates: Fill every empty room with its shortest orthogonal distance to a gate. A gate is 0, a wall is -1, and an unreachable empty room remains 2147483647. Update rooms in place.
rotting-oranges: Each minute, rotten oranges infect fresh oranges in orthogonally adjacent cells. Return the minutes needed to rot all fresh oranges, or -1 if impossible. Empty cells do not spread infection.
pacific-atlantic-water-flow: Return cells from which water can reach both the top/left borders and the bottom/right borders. Water moves orthogonally to an equal or lower height. Output coordinate order does not matter.
surrounded-regions: Change every O region that is not orthogonally connected to a border O into X. Modify board in place.
open-the-lock: Find the fewest single-wheel rotations from 0000 to target. Each wheel wraps between 0 and 9. Never enter a deadend combination. Return -1 when unreachable.
course-schedule: Determine whether all numCourses courses can be completed. A pair [a, b] means b must be completed before a.
course-schedule-ii: Return any ordering containing each course once with every prerequisite before its dependent course. Return an empty list if the prerequisites contain a cycle.
graph-valid-tree: Decide whether the undirected graph on n labeled nodes is a tree: all nodes must be connected and no cycle may exist.
course-schedule-iv: For every query [a, b], determine whether a is a direct or indirect prerequisite of b. Return answers in query order.
number-of-connected-components-in-an-und: Count the connected components of the undirected graph with nodes 0 through n-1, including isolated nodes.
redundant-connection: One extra edge was added to an undirected tree. Return an edge whose removal restores a tree; if multiple edges qualify, choose the one appearing last in the input.
accounts-merge: Merge accounts connected by a shared email address, including transitive connections. Keep the account name first and sort each account's unique emails. Result account order does not matter.
evaluate-division: Equations and values describe ratios such as a / b. Evaluate each requested ratio using the known relationships. Return -1.0 when a ratio cannot be determined, including unknown variables.
minimum-height-trees: For an undirected tree, return all root choices that minimize its rooted height. Output order does not matter.
word-ladder: Change beginWord into endWord one letter at a time, using dictionary words for every subsequent step. Return the number of words in the shortest sequence, or zero if no sequence exists.
path-with-minimum-effort: Travel orthogonally from the top-left to the bottom-right cell. A path's effort is its largest absolute height difference between consecutive cells. Return the smallest achievable effort.
network-delay-time: A signal starts at node k and follows directed weighted edges. Return the earliest time by which every node receives it, or -1 if any node is unreachable.
reconstruct-itinerary: Use every directed flight ticket exactly once to build an itinerary beginning at JFK. Choose the lexicographically smallest valid itinerary when several exist.
min-cost-to-connect-all-points: Connect all points with minimum total edge cost, where an edge costs the Manhattan distance between its endpoints. Return the minimum cost.
swim-in-rising-water: Water level equals time. Starting at the top-left cell, move orthogonally only through cells at or below the current water level. Return the earliest time the bottom-right cell is reachable.
alien-dictionary: Infer any alphabet ordering consistent with the sorted words. Include each observed character once. Return an empty string for a cycle or for a longer word preceding its exact prefix.
cheapest-flights-within-k-stops: Find the cheapest directed flight route from src to dst with at most k intermediate stops, or -1 if none exists. A route may use at most k+1 edges.
find-critical-and-pseudo-critical-edges-: Classify original edge indices into critical edges, present in every minimum spanning tree, and pseudo-critical edges, present in some but not all. Return these two groups in that order.
build-a-matrix-with-conditions: Place values 1 through k exactly once in a k by k matrix, with other cells zero. Respect rowConditions [a,b] by placing a above b and colConditions by placing a left of b. Return any valid matrix, or an empty list.
greatest-common-divisor-traversal: Indices can connect when the greatest common divisor of their values exceeds one. Decide whether all indices belong to one connected component under these connections.
climbing-stairs: Count the distinct ordered ways to reach step n when each move climbs one or two steps.
min-cost-climbing-stairs: Pay cost[i] when leaving step i, then move one or two steps. Start at step 0 or 1 and return the minimum cost to reach beyond the last step.
n-th-tribonacci-number: Return T(n) where T(0)=0, T(1)=T(2)=1, and each later value is the sum of the preceding three.
house-robber: Return the largest sum obtainable from nums without choosing adjacent positions. Choosing no position is allowed.
house-robber-ii: Return the largest sum of nonadjacent house values when the houses form a circle, so the first and last houses are also adjacent.
longest-palindromic-substring: Return any longest contiguous substring of s that reads identically in both directions.
palindromic-substrings: Count all contiguous palindromic substrings of s. Equal substrings at different positions count separately.
decode-ways: Count the ways to split the digit string into numbers 1 through 26 representing letters. A leading zero cannot form a letter, and standalone zero is invalid.
coin-change: Return the smallest number of coins needed to make amount, with unlimited copies of each denomination. Return -1 when impossible and zero for amount zero.
maximum-product-subarray: Return the maximum product among nonempty contiguous subarrays of nums. Negative values and zero are allowed.
word-break: Decide whether s can be split completely into dictionary words. Each dictionary word may be used multiple times.
longest-increasing-subsequence: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of nums. A subsequence preserves order but need not be contiguous.
partition-equal-subset-sum: Determine whether nums can be split into two groups with equal sums, using every value exactly once.
combination-sum-iv: Count the ordered sequences of positive numbers from nums that sum to target. Each number may be reused, and different orders count separately.
perfect-squares: Return the fewest perfect-square positive integers whose sum is n. Squares may repeat.
integer-break: Split n into at least two positive integers and return the largest possible product of those integers.
stone-game-iii: Players alternate taking the next one, two, or three stones from the front. Each gains their taken values. Assuming optimal play, return Alice, Bob, or Tie according to the final scores.
unique-paths: Count routes from the top-left to the bottom-right of an m by n grid, moving only right or down.
unique-paths-ii: Count right/down routes through obstacleGrid from the top-left to the bottom-right. A 1 cell blocks movement; a 0 cell is open.
minimum-path-sum: Find the minimum sum along a path from the top-left to the bottom-right, moving only right or down and including both endpoint values.
longest-common-subsequence: Return the length of the longest sequence appearing in both text1 and text2 in the same order, not necessarily contiguously.
last-stone-weight-ii: Repeatedly smash any two stones, replacing them with their absolute weight difference. Return the smallest final weight achievable, treating no remaining stone as zero.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-with-coo: Maximize stock profit with any number of transactions while holding at most one share. After selling, you must wait one full day before buying again.
coin-change-ii: Count distinct combinations of unlimited coin denominations that total amount. Different orders of the same coins count once. Amount zero has one empty combination.
target-sum: Assign either a plus or minus sign to each nums occurrence. Count assignments whose signed sum equals target.
interleaving-string: Decide whether s3 can be formed by interleaving s1 and s2 while preserving the order of characters within each original string.
stone-game: Two optimal players alternately take the leftmost or rightmost pile. There are an even number of piles and an odd total stone count. Return whether the first player wins.
stone-game-ii: Players take the next X piles, where 1 <= X <= 2M and M begins at 1. After a turn M becomes max(M,X). Return the largest number of stones the first player can secure against optimal play.
longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing path through orthogonally adjacent matrix cells. Diagonal moves are disallowed.
distinct-subsequences: Count ways to delete characters from s so the remaining sequence equals t. Different selections of source positions count separately.
edit-distance: Return the smallest number of single-character insertions, deletions, and replacements that transform word1 into word2.
burst-balloons: Choose an order to burst every balloon. Bursting one earns its value times the values of its current neighbors; a missing neighbor has value 1. Return the greatest total score.
regular-expression-matching: Match the entire string s against pattern p. A dot matches one character; a star repeats the preceding token zero or more times. This is full-string matching, not substring search.
lemonade-change: Customers pay in order for an item costing 5 using bills of 5, 10, or 20. Starting with no change, determine whether each customer can receive exact change immediately.
maximum-subarray: Return the largest sum of any nonempty contiguous subarray of nums.
maximum-sum-circular-subarray: Return the greatest sum of a nonempty contiguous subarray when nums wraps around from its end to its start. Each element can be used at most once.
longest-turbulent-subarray: Return the longest contiguous length whose neighboring comparisons alternate strictly between greater-than and less-than. Equal adjacent values break the pattern.
jump-game: nums[i] is the maximum forward jump length from index i. Decide whether the final index can be reached from index zero.
jump-game-ii: Return the fewest forward jumps needed to reach the last index. From i you may advance up to nums[i] positions, and reaching the end is guaranteed possible.
jump-game-vii: Start at index zero of a binary string. Jump between minJump and maxJump positions forward, landing only on 0. Decide whether the last index is reachable.
gas-station: Each circular-route station supplies gas[i], and traveling to the next costs cost[i]. Return a starting index that completes a full circuit without negative fuel, or -1. A valid start is unique.
hand-of-straights: Decide whether all cards can be divided into groups of groupSize consecutive integer values. Each card occurrence is used once.
dota2-senate: Senators act cyclically, and each active senator bans an opposing senator from future turns. Assuming optimal choices, return Radiant or Dire for the surviving party.
merge-triplets-to-form-target-triplet: You may replace one triplet with the coordinate-wise maximum of it and another triplet. Decide whether target can be obtained from the supplied triplets.
partition-labels: Split s into the greatest possible number of consecutive segments so each letter occurs in only one segment. Return the segment lengths.
valid-parenthesis-string: Decide whether s can be balanced by treating each star as an opening parenthesis, a closing parenthesis, or an empty string.
candy: Give every child at least one candy. A child with a higher rating than an immediate neighbor must receive more candy than that neighbor. Return the minimum total.
insert-interval: Insert newInterval into a sorted list of nonoverlapping intervals, merging any overlaps. Return the resulting sorted intervals.
merge-intervals: Merge all overlapping closed intervals and return the resulting nonoverlapping intervals sorted by start. Touching closed endpoints overlap.
non-overlapping-intervals: Return the minimum number of intervals to remove so none overlap. An interval ending exactly when another begins does not conflict.
meeting-rooms: Decide whether a person can attend every meeting without overlap. A meeting may begin exactly when another ends.
meeting-rooms-ii: Return the fewest rooms required to hold all meetings. A room becomes available at a meeting's end time.
meeting-rooms-iii: Assign meetings to n rooms, preferring the smallest available room number. If all are occupied, delay a meeting until the earliest room frees, preserving duration and original start order. Return the busiest room, breaking count ties by smallest number.
minimum-interval-to-include-each-query: For every query value, return the length of the smallest closed interval containing it, or -1. Interval length is right-left+1. Preserve query order.
excel-sheet-column-title: Convert a positive column number to spreadsheet letters: 1 is A, 26 is Z, 27 is AA, and so on.
greatest-common-divisor-of-strings: Return the longest nonempty string whose repetitions form both str1 and str2, or an empty string when no such divisor exists.
insert-greatest-common-divisors-in-linke: Between each adjacent pair of linked-list nodes, insert a new node holding the greatest common divisor of their values. Return the head.
transpose-matrix: Return the matrix transpose: rows of the input become columns of the output.
rotate-image: Rotate the square matrix 90 degrees clockwise in place, without allocating another matrix.
spiral-matrix: Return matrix elements in clockwise spiral order, beginning at the top-left and moving right.
set-matrix-zeroes: If an input cell is zero, set its entire row and column to zero. Apply this simultaneously based on original zeros and modify the matrix in place.
happy-number: Repeatedly replace n with the sum of the squares of its decimal digits. Return True if the sequence reaches 1, and False if it enters another cycle.
plus-one: digits contains a nonnegative integer in most-significant-digit-first order. Return its digit array after adding one.
roman-to-integer: Convert a valid Roman numeral to an integer, accounting for subtractive pairs such as IV and IX.
powx-n: Compute x raised to the integer exponent n, including negative exponents. Target logarithmic time in the absolute exponent.
multiply-strings: Multiply two nonnegative integers represented as decimal strings and return the decimal product. Do not convert the entire strings to built-in integers or use big-integer multiplication.
detect-squares: Implement DetectSquares.add(point) and count(point). Count axis-aligned squares with positive area using the query point and three previously added points. Duplicate stored points multiply the number of choices.
single-number: Every nums value occurs twice except one that occurs once. Return the unpaired value using linear time and constant extra space.
number-of-1-bits: Return the number of set bits in the binary representation of n.
counting-bits: Return a list of length n+1 where position i contains the number of set bits in i.
add-binary: Return the binary-string sum of the binary strings a and b.
reverse-bits: Reverse all 32 bits of the unsigned integer n, preserving leading zero positions in the 32-bit representation.
missing-number: nums contains distinct values drawn from 0 through n, with one value absent. Return the missing value.
sum-of-two-integers: Return a+b without using the addition or subtraction operators. Inputs and output follow signed 32-bit integer arithmetic.
reverse-integer: Reverse the decimal digits of signed integer x while preserving its sign. Return zero when the reversed result lies outside the signed 32-bit range.
bitwise-and-of-numbers-range: Return the bitwise AND of every integer from left through right, inclusive.
minimum-array-end: Choose a strictly increasing sequence of n positive integers whose bitwise AND is x. Return the smallest possible final element.
